name: IPIP emotional intelligence components
items_note: Items copied from https://ipip.ori.org/newEmotionalIntelligenceKey.htm, 3 November 2026. The key page lists items by scale without an administration order; the items here are interleaved across the scales in round-robin order.

source.paper: Barchard, K. A. (2001). Emotional and social intelligence: Examining its place in the nomological network. Unpublished doctoral dissertation, University of British Columbia. Scales reproduced in the International Personality Item Pool

licence.text: Public domain (IPIP). Permission is granted automatically for any person to use IPIP items for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial.

instructions: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age.

items.text: Express my affection physically.
Shout or scream when I'm angry.
Think about the causes of my emotions.
Listen to my feelings when making important decisions.
Like to watch children open presents.
Am deeply moved by others' misfortunes.
Am concerned about others.
Laugh out loud if something is funny.
Can't help but look upset when something bad happens.
Pay a lot of attention to my feelings.
Base my goals in life on inspiration, rather than logic.

Am easily moved to tears.
Feel sympathy for those who are worse off than myself.
Express my happiness in a childlike manner.
Show my fear.

Feel other people's joy.
Suffer from others' sorrows.
Sympathize with the homeless.
Sometimes laugh out loud when reading or watching TV.

Notice my emotions.

Hug my close friends.
Show my sadness.

Am unaffected by other people's happiness.
Am unaffected by the suffering of others.
Look down on any weakness.

reliabilitySource: Coefficient alpha per scale from the IPIP key page, which gives two figures per scale (women and men); the lower of the two is stored here. Women/men: positive expressivity .81/.79, negative expressivity .75/.74, attending to emotions .81/.83, emotion-based decision-making .73/.67, responsive joy .73/.70, responsive distress .59/.63, empathic concern .64/.80.
